STEP 1 - Scene: A side dish of cooked sliced carrots (glazed or braised, with a light sauce), served on its own.

STEP 2 - Vessel: A white square plate, roughly 22 cm across. Area ≈ 22 x 22 x ~0.85 (rounded corners) ≈ 410 cm^2. Treat as a side plate, about 20 cm diameter equivalent, area ≈ 314 cm^2 for the round-equivalent estimate. I use 350 cm^2 as a compromise for the square plate.

STEP 3 - Items: Cooked carrot coins/slices with a glaze or light sauce. No other foods visible.

STEP 4 - Area: Carrots cover roughly 30% of the plate, concentrated in the center-right. Sauce is only a thin film, included in the carrots.

STEP 5 - Volume: 350 cm^2 x 30% = 105 cm^2 covered. Typical pile height about 2 cm (carrot slices stacked a few layers deep). Gross volume ≈ 105 x 2 = 210 ml.

STEP 6 - Grams: Cut vegetables bulk density ~0.6 g/ml. 210 ml x 0.6 ≈ 126 g.

STEP 7 - Energy: Cooked carrots ≈ 35 kcal/100 g; a glaze adds some sugar and fat, so use ~50 kcal/100 g as plated. 126 g x 0.5 ≈ 63 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: About 20 carrot pieces on a side plate, roughly 125 g, is plausible for a visible side portion. Total ≈ 126 g, ≈ 63 kcal.

Summary: about 126 g of glazed carrots, roughly 60–65 kcal.
